item.title: Russia’s ambassador to the US dies ‘suddenly’, foreign ministry says
item.description: Russia’s ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, has died “suddenly” at the age of 66 after just one and a half years in the job, Moscow’s foreign ministry announced on Wednesday. The ministry called Darchiev an “outstanding diplomat, an experienced leader and a kind colleague”. He was appointed in March 2025. Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said in a separate statement that Darchiev died in Moscow from an unspecified chronic illness. Darchiev previously served as Russia’s...

item.title: Rubio, Wang hold phone call before Xi-Trump meeting next week

item.title: Russia, Ukraine agree on prisoner exchange as talks end without major breakthrough
item.description: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war, both sides said Wednesday as two days of US mediated talks concluded, but they announced no major breakthrough on ending the conflict that began after Moscow’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago. Hopes had been low for any significant development in the first meeting in nine months between the delegations. item.title: How are Chinese infantry units training to survive drone-filled battlefields?
item.description: China’s infantry units are adapting to the growing threat from drones, with some brigades introducing compulsory counter-drone training, new equipment and fresh tactics to help soldiers evade aerial surveillance and attacks. The latest example comes from a brigade of the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) 75th Group Army, which has made counter-drone training compulsory after an exercise exposed how troops relying on traditional camouflage were vulnerable to drone-directed artillery...

item.title: Google in, but Nvidia out as US lines up Apec CEO Summit delegation: source
item.description: Representatives from Google and Boeing will be included in the United States’ business delegation at next week’s Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen, the event organiser has confirmed. But a source familiar with the arrangements said Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was unlikely to attend at this stage, with many high-profile executives yet to confirm their participation.
